mythologySignificance:
Pandharpur’s Vitthal-Rukmini temple is the heart of the Warkari tradition of Maharashtra. Vitthal is worshipped as a form of Krishna/Vishnu standing on a brick — a theology sung in the Abhangas of saints from Namdev and Dnyaneshwar to Tukaram.

Pilgrimage literature treats Vitthal-Rukmini Temple, Pandharpur as a tirtha — a crossing where devotion to Lord Vitthal (Vithoba) & Rukmini is believed to bear fruit more readily than in ordinary space. Accounts summarised here follow widely cited epic, Puranic, and regional mahatmya traditions; temple priests remain the guides for ritual detail.
localBeliefs:
Ashadhi and Kartiki Ekadashi pilgrimages (wari) — barefoot processions of palakhis from across Maharashtra — are the living scripture of Pandharpur. Devotees believe Vitthal waits eternally for the bhakta.

Standing with hands on hips, the murti’s posture itself is read as welcoming the weary pilgrim.
